2027-04-14.title: Wednesday of the Third Week of Easter
readings: Those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word; there was great joy in that city
Let all the earth cry out to God with joy (or: Alleluia)
This is the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life
2027-04-14.alt: Easter weekday. The Alleluia sounds again at the Gospel acclamation; the Paschal candle is lit at the liturgy until Pentecost; the Regina Caeli takes the place of the Angelus. All this week the Gospel is the Bread of Life discourse of John 6. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-14.verse: This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.
theo: The day Stephen died, “a severe persecution began against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout the countryside of Judea and Samaria.” It looks like the end of the young Church. Devout men bury Stephen “and made loud lamentation over him”; Christian mourning is real mourning, even when it is full of hope. Saul goes from house to house, dragging off men and women to prison. And then St Luke writes one of the most hopeful sentences in the Acts of the Apostles: “Now those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word.” The persecution that was meant to stamp out the Church scatters it like seed. Before his Ascension the risen Lord had said: “you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth” (Acts 1:8). The disciples had stayed in Jerusalem; now, through suffering, the word moves into Judea and Samaria exactly as he said. Tertullian would later write, in substance, that the blood of Christians is seed. Philip, one of the Seven like Stephen, goes down to a city of Samaria. Jews and Samaritans had kept apart for centuries (John 4:9), yet here “the crowds with one accord listened eagerly” to Philip; unclean spirits come out, the paralyzed and the lame are healed, “so there was great joy in that city.” The Psalm becomes the song of Samaria: “Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth… Come and see what God has done.” Kerala knows this story well. Malayali Catholics scattered by work and need across the Gulf, Europe, America and every corner of India have often carried the faith with them and planted it where they went: a rosary group in a labour camp, a Malayalam Mass in a borrowed chapel, a family that keeps praying in a foreign city.

In the Gospel Jesus repeats the great word of yesterday, “I am the bread of life,” and then opens his heart about the will of his Father. “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.” No one who comes to him is turned away: not the sinner, not the doubter, not the one who comes late. Then he speaks of his own obedience: “I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.” Here we glimpse the mystery St Martin I defended: the Son made man has a true human will, and he freely and lovingly makes it one with the Father's will (Catechism 475). And what is that will? “That I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day.” Four times in this chapter Jesus says “I will raise them up on the last day.” The Easter faith is not a vague survival of the soul; it is the resurrection of the body, our own bodies raised and glorified like his. And the Bread of Life is bound to that promise: those who receive the Eucharist receive, as the Catechism says, a pledge of future glory (Catechism 1402–1405). This is the hope with which the devout men buried Stephen, and the hope with which the Church buries her children still: the Lord who feeds us will not lose us.
outline: Ask: what good has God brought out of a time when my life was scattered?
Persecution carries the word to Samaria.
Point 2 · Great joy in that city
Point 3 · I will never drive away
Anyone who comes to Jesus is received.
Point 4 · Raised on the last day
“I will raise them up on the last day.”
live: If you live away from home, find one way this week to share the faith where you are: invite a fellow migrant to Mass, or start a short family prayer.
Bring to Jesus today the thing you are most ashamed of. He has promised not to drive you away; go to confession if you need to.
2027-04-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, bread of life, you turned the scattering of your Church into the spreading of your word, and you fill whole cities with joy. Receive all who come to you, lose none of those the Father has given you, and raise us up on the last day to see your face. Amen. Alleluia.
altar: The Father wills that none be lost. In the Eucharist the risen Lord gives us his own glorified Body as the pledge of our resurrection: the one who feeds us now will raise us up on the last day.

quick: After Stephen's death the believers were scattered, and wherever they went they proclaimed the word.
Philip preached Christ in Samaria, and there was great joy in that city.
Jesus said: anyone who comes to me I will never drive away, and I will raise them up on the last day.
2027-04-14.action: Bring to Jesus today something you have been afraid to bring him.
2027-04-14.question: Where has God turned a scattering in my life into a sowing?

family.explain: Jesus said a beautiful thing: anyone who comes to me, I will never send away. Even if we have done something wrong, even if we feel small or sad, Jesus is always happy when we come to him. And he promised that on the last day he will raise us up, so that we live with him for ever.
family.intention: We pray for families who live far from home, especially our relatives working abroad.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family lives far away? Let us call or message them this week and pray for them by name.”

illus: A nurse from Pala went to work in a hospital in a small German town where there was no Malayali family and no Mass in any language she knew. For the first months she cried after every night shift. Then she began to pray the rosary aloud in the hospital chapel at five in the morning. A Filipino cleaner joined her, then a Polish doctor, then a nurse from Kerala who had stopped practising her faith years before. When the parish priest found six people praying in three languages, he asked them to read at the Sunday Mass.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you drive no one away. We come to you just as we are. Fill us with the joy of Samaria. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word (Acts 8:4). How can my difficulties become a way of spreading the Gospel?
So there was great joy in that city (Acts 8:8). Where have I seen the joy that Christ brings to a place?
Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37). Is there someone I keep at a distance whom Jesus would welcome?
pm.resp: Let all the earth cry out to God with joy. Alleluia.
interc: For Christians scattered by persecution or war, that they may carry the word wherever they go.
For Malayali migrants and all who work far from home, and for the families they support.
For deacons, catechists and missionaries who, like Philip, bring Christ to new places.
For those who think Jesus would turn them away, that they may come to him without fear.
For our beloved dead, that the Lord may raise them up on the last day.
pm.close: Father, your will is that none be lost. Keep us close to your Son, the bread of life, and bring us all to the resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, after Stephen's death it seemed that everything was falling apart. A great persecution began, and believers fled from Jerusalem in every direction. But St Luke says: those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word (Acts 8:4). The wind that was meant to blow out the fire only carried its sparks further.

Philip went to Samaria, a people the Jews had kept apart from for centuries. He proclaimed Christ, the sick were healed, and so there was great joy in that city (Acts 8:8). God's word does not stay within our walls. Many of you know what it is to be scattered: for work, for study, for family. Wherever you go, you take the word with you.

In the Gospel Jesus says something every one of us needs to hear: anyone who comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37). Not the one who has failed, not the one who has been away for years. And he tells us the Father's will: that he should lose nothing of what the Father has given him, but raise it up on the last day.

That is our Easter hope. Not only that our souls live on, but that our bodies will be raised. Every time we receive the Bread of Life, we receive the pledge of that resurrection. So let us come to him without fear, and carry his joy wherever life scatters us. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: I will never send away anyone who comes to me. That means you can always come to Jesus: when you are happy, when you are sad, even when you have been naughty! He always opens his arms. Let us run to him today and say: Jesus, here I am!

intro: Theme: “I will raise them up on the last day.”
The scattering that became a sowing, the joy of Samaria, and the Lord who drives no one away.

sub: The word goes into Judea and Samaria.
q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
Now those who were scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word.
points.apply: Offer to God one painful change in your life this week and ask him to make it fruitful for the Gospel.

q: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth; sing the glory of his name; give to him glorious praise.
So there was great joy in that city.
points.apply: Bring the joy of Easter to one place this week where there is little joy: a hospital, a lonely home, a tense office.

q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak
This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.
points.apply: Invite back, gently and personally, one person who has drifted away from the Church.

concl: God turns the scattering of his people into the spreading of his word and the joy of new cities.
Jesus receives all who come to him and will raise them up on the last day.
2027-04-14.resolve: Pray this week for one person far from home and one person far from the Church, and reach out to each.
